text:
maya: hey team — hitting a weird tokenization/toolcall mismatch when bringing up an HF chat model via hf->rw conversion. tool tags get eaten in JSON-mode. anyone seen this?

ethan: seen similar. can you paste a minimal example of the toolcall payload + tokenizer config?

maya: sure, here's the failing convo and tokenizer dump:

```
User: run_calculator
{"tool_call": {"name": "calc", "args": {"expr": "2+2"}}}
```

tokenizer.tokens: ["run", "_", "calc", "{", "\u201c", "tool_call", "\u201d", ":", "{" , "name" ...] — note the smart quotes and braces split. the model returns something like: `\u201c{\u201d` broken across tokens, so JSON parsing fails after generation.

jia: probable cause: HF tokenizer doesn't know about our special tool markers (tool tags, JSON-mode sentinels, role tokens). during convert we need to inject added_special_tokens and ensure the pre-tokenizer normalisation preserves the sentinel characters.

sam: quick checklist i follow: add tokenizers.added_special_tokens = ["<|tool_call|>", "</tool_call>", "<JSON_MODE>", "</JSON_MODE>", "<|role_system|>", "<|role_assistant|>"] and set tokenizers.normalizer to not do NFKC on those ranges.

oliver: note: quantization experiments revealed another gotcha — some byte-level BPE merges change how long sentinel tokens are split, so after int8 quant we saw the sentinel split into 3 tokens at generation time. that only shows up at certain seqlen distributions.

infra-bot: convert-bot: conversion job 1790502468 finished with warnings: 2 special tokens unmapped -> see job logs (link) :warning:

maya: i patched the tokenizer locally and re-ran conversion. patch diff: 

```
"added_special_tokens": ["<|tool_call|>", "</tool_call>", "<JSON_START_⟨01⟩>", "<JSON_END_⟨01⟩>", "<|role_system|>", "<|role_user|>"]
"redwood_chat_role_tokens": true
```

that stopped the token splits for the tool payload in our test prompts, JSON parsed cleanly in 95/100 runs.

ethan: good. also make sure convert flags include `--preserve-role-tokens` and `--inject-special-tokens`. converters sometimes drop tokens if they think they are unknown.

jia: another trick: use private-use unicode sentinels (U+E000..U+E0FF) for JSON mode if you can guarantee the tokenizer maps them as a single token. less chance of collision with user text. example payload: 

```
<E000>
{"tool_call": {"name": "calc", "args": {"expr": "2+2"}}}
<E001>
```

sam: i tested that: using U+E000/U+E001 pair plus adding them to added_special_tokens fixed ambiguity. watch out though — some downstream export tools strip non-ascii chars.

oliver: for tests: add a roundtrip tokenization unit test: tokenise->detokenise on tool blocks and assert parsed JSON equals input. also add a fuzz test where random whitespace or smart quotes are inserted. caught several regressions for me.

maya: the failing evals i saw were small but consistent: after int8 quant we get ~2% JSON syntax error rate in our JSON-mode eval set. looks like quantization indirectly changed generation tokenization boundaries.

ethan: question — do we keep role tokens embedded in the stream (e.g., `<|role_system|>`) or strip them and rely on RW chatfmt metadata? runtime expects role tokens if model was trained with them; if not, runtime will inject them at formatting stage. mixing both is dangerous.

jia: rule of thumb: if model's training data contained explicit role tokens, preserve them. else prefer runtime-injected role markers. Document this in model card under `redwood_conversion_notes`.

sam: small practical tip: when you add special tokens run `tokenizer.unique_no_split_tokens` so BPE doesn't merge them. also lock merges for those tokens in tokenizer.json.

maya: thanks — will make those edits, add roundtrip tests and re-run quant experiments. i'll post results here.

oliver: :thumbsup: also update onboarding checklist in `eng-ml/model-onboard-checklist.md` with steps: inject-special-tokens, run token roundtrip tests, run json-mode evals, run quantization smoke test.

maya: will do.

ethan: FYI i added a small helper script `scripts/convert_hf_to_rw_fix_specials.py` that automates patching tokenizer.json + model card fields. ping me if you want it.

maya: pinging you for the script, thanks!
